what_this_is: One name per model, and the ONLY place the correspondence between the two pipelines is written down. QM9 (process_and_train.py -> models/models.py -> save_results) and the laboratory runner (KIRBy tests/alternative_data_noise_robustness.py) each write their own spelling into the `model` column, and every table that puts the four datasets side by side joins on that string. A second naming rule anywhere means the two cannot be joined -- which is exactly what happened to the four models added on 2026-08-28.
why_it_exists: scripts/generate_paper_figures_v2.py held the laboratory-to-canonical map inline (val_model_map) and the QM9-to-canonical map inline beside it (BNN_NAME_MAP), and neither was updated when GP-Tanimoto, GP-Hetero, VBLL-Full-Hetero and MLP-VBLL-Full-Hetero started being emitted. An unmapped name does not raise: `.fillna(df['model'].str.lower())` turns 'GP-Hetero' into 'gp-hetero', which is a model name nothing else in the study uses, so the row survives into the frame under a name that joins to nothing. scripts/uncertainty_stats.py did not normalise model names at ALL, so the pooled uncertainty frame carried 'het_gp_rbf' and 'GP-Hetero' as two different models. This is the same failure condition_names.json exists to stop for noise conditions, and it gets the same treatment: one file, read by both consumers, checked by a test.
the_rule: `canonical` is what every figure, table and statistic uses. `qm9` maps what models/models.py passes to save_results; `validation` maps the display name the laboratory runner builds its experiment list with. Hyphen-stripped spellings are accepted automatically by the reader (the per-molecule uncertainty FILENAMES strip hyphens), so they are not listed here.

notes.GP: The laboratory runner names the ordinary process by its kernel: 'GP' when the kernel is RBF, 'GP-Tanimoto' otherwise. QM9 names the same two models gauche_rbf and gauche. They are DIFFERENT models -- an RBF kernel on any representation against a Tanimoto kernel on binary fingerprints only -- and mapping both to one name would pool two kernels into one row.
notes.hetero: The -Hetero / _hetero suffix means the observation noise is predicted per molecule instead of being one number per fit. It is load-bearing and must not be folded into the plain name: the two report different KINDS of data-noise term, and a per-molecule column and a broadcast constant would become indistinguishable (RERUN_PLAN.md 5.5f).
notes.dnn_prefix: The QM9 DNN trainer writes the Bayesian variants WITHOUT a base prefix ('bnn_full'), while the MLP trainer writes them WITH one ('mlp_bnn_full'). Both spellings are listed rather than fixed in models.py, because changing what the pipeline writes would orphan every results file already on disk.
